summary: When someone speaks to Nora in a Discord voice channel, her music controls are already loaded, so a spoken request to play, stop, change the volume, move a track up or check what is playing no longer waits for an extra lookup step first.
details: Which tools stay loaded on spoken turns is declared on each tool and chosen from measured use: five music controls were called on 14 of 26 spoken turns between 17 and 30 September.
Typed turns are unchanged, in every room.
limitations: Skipping a track was never asked for by voice in that window, so it still loads on demand.

Each spoken turn carries about 660 more tokens of tool descriptions, and spoken and typed turns no longer share the same cached prompt prefix; the latency and cost effect has been estimated from recorded turns, not yet measured before and after.
